source_refs.note: Exercise 10.1, Question 6: book page 278 (Q1-Q24). The book prints no answers for Exercise 10.1.

blocks.explanation:
Is equation mein ek hi angle ke \(\sin^{2}x\) aur \(\cos^{2}x\) hain. Agar poori equation ko \(\cos^{2}x\) se divide kar dein to sirf ek ratio, \(\tan x\), bachta hai.
Find kya karna hai? Principal solutions aur general solution.
Lekin divide karne se pehle ek ehtiyaat: dekhna hai ke \(\cos x = 0\) khud jawab to nahin, warna divide karne se woh gum ho jata.
Plan: check, divide, \(\tan x = \pm\sqrt{3}\) hal karo, period \(\pi\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sin^{2}x - 3\cos^{2}x = 0\).
Maloom karna: principal solutions aur general solution.
Tareeqa: \(\cos^{2}x\) se divide kar ke sirf \(\tan x\) wali equation banayenge, kyunke \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x\).

Kya \(\cos x = 0\) ho sakta hai?
Agar \(\cos x = 0\) ho to \(\sin^{2}x = 1\) aur left side \(1 - 0 = 1 \ne 0\).
Kyun: kisi variable expression se divide karne se pehle yeh dekhna zaroori hai ke us ke zero hone par koi jawab to nahin chhup raha. Yahan nahin chhupa, is liye divide karna mehfooz hai.

\(\cos^{2}x\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{\cos^{2}x} - 3 = 0\]
\[\tan^{2}x = 3\]
\[\tan x = \pm\sqrt{3}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{\sin^{2}x}{\cos^{2}x} = \tan^{2}x\) aur \(\frac{3\cos^{2}x}{\cos^{2}x} = 3\). Square root ke saath \(\pm\) zaroori hai.

Jab \(\tan x = \sqrt{3}\) (quadrant I, III)
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
\[x = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: tangent quadrant I aur III mein positive hai.

Jab \(\tan x = -\sqrt{3}\) (quadrant II, IV)
\[x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\]
\[x = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: tangent quadrant II aur IV mein negative hai.

General solution
Tangent ka period \(\pi\) hai, aur \(\frac{4\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{3} + \pi\), \(\frac{5\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3} + \pi\):
\[\left\{\dfrac{\pi}{3} + n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{2\pi}{3} + n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Kyun: tangent har \(\pi\) ke baad dohrata hai, is liye do families chaaron jawab samet leti hain.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}:\ \dfrac{3}{4} - 3\cdot\dfrac{1}{4} = 0\]
Kyun: \(\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) aur \(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\). Baqi teen angles par bhi \(\sin^{2}x = \frac{3}{4}\) aur \(\cos^{2}x = \frac{1}{4}\) hain, to wahan bhi zero aata hai.
Dhyan dein: doosra tareeqa bhi hai: \(\cos^{2}x = 1 - \sin^{2}x\) rakhein to \(4\sin^{2}x = 3\), yani \(\sin x = \pm\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), aur wahi chaar angles milte hain (Question 4 jaise).
blocks.final_answer: Principal solutions \([0, 2\pi]\) mein: \(x = \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{2\pi}{3}, \frac{4\pi}{3}, \frac{5\pi}{3}\). General solution: \(\left\{\frac{\pi}{3} + n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{2\pi}{3} + n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 10.1 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain. Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. Kitab ke examples ki tarah hum principal solutions \([0, 2\pi]\) mein aur general solution sets ke union ki shakal mein dete hain. Aap apna kaam yahan wale hal se mila kar dekh sakte hain.
